thread:
maria: evening slice kickoff — US -> EU -> APAC. target change window 21:00-23:30 PT. canary plan: US 1% -> 5% -> 25% then full if clean.
liam: noted. warm pools checked? any thermal constraints in apac tonight?
ajay: warm pools: us 220/300 GPUs available, eu 60/120, apac 30/80 (see ops-bot summary below). we should keep apac at manual hold until us/eu finish.
ops-bot: capacity snapshot: US(us-west-2): free=220, total=300; EU(eu-west-1): free=60, total=120; APAC(ap-northeast-1): free=30, total=80. fetch command: ```opsctl capacity --regions us,eu,apac --format short```
release-manager: release notes uploaded: https://docs.internal/release-notes/2026-03-21. tl;dr: v1.2.3 model-serving changes, routing fallback improvements, a small perf regressed case (rolling guardrails added). marketing looped.
sophie: monitoring: I'm on dash and alerts. thresholds: error_rate > 1.5% over 5m OR p95 > 500ms for 3m triggers rollback. I'll post early if anything noisy.
maria: @deploy-bot, start US canary 1% slice now. pin version to v1.2.3 for the canary. keep previous model variant as fallback.
deploy-bot: starting canary: region=us, percent=1, version=v1.2.3, fallback=v1.2.2-slot. canary_id=cb-1718901234.
liam: seeing slight queue growth in us-west-2 tokens (10% above baseline) — not alarming yet. holding progression until we see stability for 10m.
ajay: agree. hold on 5% step until 10m stable signals. can we enable KV-cache warmup for the canary?
maria: yes enable prefix caching for canary. small config: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood/svc/cache/warm -d '{"canary_id":"cb-1718901234","regions":["us"]}'```
sophie: dashboard check 5m in: error_rate=0.12%, p95=210ms, cpu at 68% — looking good.
ops-bot: thermal check: no thermal throttles flagged in US pools. EU pools nominal. APAC cooling schedule at 02:00 local — keep manual hold.
deploy-bot: progression gated: US -> waiting 10m stability before 5% step. ETA next decision +10m.
liam: small prod log noise: transient 429s from a downstream retrier; not user-facing. I'll mute noisy alert and follow up with the service owner.
release-manager: quick note for support: pinned customers doc updated with rollback command snippet and contact list. snippet: ```# rollback canary
redwoodctl rollout cancel --id cb-1718901234 --region us
redwoodctl promote --version v1.2.2 --region us
```
maria: if rollback needed, we follow staged rollback: cancel canary, promote fallback, then open incident and schedule a controlled sweep to roll back EU if it hit there.
sophie: 15m mark: still clean. I'm green for 5% step unless others object.
ajay: go for 5% in US. EU still on hold until we validate telemetry for 30m at 5%.
deploy-bot: stepping canary to 5% in US (canary_id cb-1718901234 -> step=5).
liam: monitor queue and token latency. I'll watch for p95 jumps > 100ms from baseline.
ops-bot: updated capacity: US free=210/300, EU free=58/120, APAC free=30/80. no immediate capacity pressure.
sophie: 5% stable for 12m now. error_rate=0.18%, p95=230ms. green to schedule EU canary at 1% but keep EU manual hold for now until 30m US stability.
maria: agreed. APAC remains manual. release-manager: I will broadcast progress to #announcements after EU 1% start. short note: "rolling update v1.2.3 — US 5% stable; EU and APAC staged; watch ops channel for live updates."
liam: FYI if we see any CPU thermal trend in apac we'll keep the manual hold and use regional fallback routing to keep user latency low.
ops-bot: final snapshot at end of thread: US free=208, EU free=57, APAC free=30.
release-manager: thanks all — next checkin 20m or earlier if anything pops. :thumbsup:
